title: 5dot: A Cross-Platform Mobile App That Detects AI-Generated Voice, Video and Lip-Sync
headline: Know what's real: check any clip in minutes
summary: A React Native app for iOS and Android that checks a video or audio clip for AI-cloned voices, deepfake video and lip-sync tampering, and explains the verdict in plain language.
problem: AI-generated and edited media spreads fast, and ordinary people have no simple way to check whether a clip is genuine. The client needed a polished consumer app for iOS and Android, from first screen to app-store release.
solution: I built the entire mobile app: 10 screens and 6 shared components, implemented from Figma designs. Users upload a video or audio file or paste a link, pick which checks to run (AI voice, AI video, lip-sync), and get a plain-language verdict with a confidence score. An expandable, per-segment chart shows the raw signal for anyone who wants to see it. The detection itself runs on a Python API built by a separate backend developer; I connected the app to it and handled everything on the device and in the release pipeline.
highlights: Upload or link a video or audio file, then run one or more detectors
Plain-language verdict with a filterable per-segment score chart, drawn with custom SVG
Sign in with email and one-time code, Google, or Apple, with tokens kept in the device's secure storage and refreshed silently
Scan history you can filter by verdict, detection type and status, plus weekly usage and quota tracking
Free, Pro and Team plans with feature gating
Push notifications on iOS and Android, crash reporting, and a remote switch to force old app versions to update
Built, signed and submitted for both the App Store and Google Play
role: Sole mobile and full-stack engineer on an extended freelance engagement. I owned the whole React Native app end to end, the native build and release pipeline for both app stores, the third-party integrations, and ongoing features and fixes. A separate backend developer built the Python API; I worked alongside them.

results.label: Release pipelines for both iOS and Android working end to end
Google Play's new 16 KB memory-page requirement resolved, unblocking new releases
Push notifications live on both iOS and Android
Sign in with Apple, Google or email, with secure token storage

challenges.title: Google Play rejected new releases
challenges.text: Prebuilt native libraries from an older Expo SDK weren't compiled with the 16 KB memory-page alignment Android now requires. I scoped and carried out an Expo SDK 52 to 54 upgrade, and confirmed it was enough by inspecting the alignment inside the compiled Android bundle instead of guessing.

challenges.title: The iOS build broke after the upgrade
challenges.text: Five separate native toolchain problems stacked up: outdated per-library iOS deployment targets, an incompatible Kotlin and NDK pin, a Clang non-modular-include error under static framework linking, Firebase's move to Swift Package Manager clashing with that linking, and React Native's new prebuilt core failing to link one dependency. I diagnosed each from the raw Xcode and Gradle logs and fixed them with targeted Expo config plugins and build-time settings, without rolling the upgrade back.

challenges.title: The Android build broke on the Firebase upgrade
challenges.text: The Firebase library's own bundled Kotlin code passed a nullable value into a React Native API that now requires a non-null one. I patched the three affected lines with patch-package and hooked it into postinstall, so the fix survives the fresh installs on every future cloud build.

challenges.title: The new logo had no transparent version
challenges.text: A 3D-rendered brand refresh came with no cutout, and its dark background was almost the same colour as the logo's own empty space. I separated the mark from the background programmatically by its colour saturation (vivid rings against a grey backdrop) instead of asking for a redo.
